## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fóshuō Píngshā wáng wǔyuàn jīng* (T511) is a one-fascicle short sūtra by [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) Zhī Qiān. The protagonist *Píngshā* 蓱沙 is a Chinese phonetic transliteration of *Bimbisāra* — the king of Magadha and a major patron of the Buddha (also father of Ajātaśatru, cf. [KR6i0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0137)–[KR6i0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0139)). The text narrates Bimbisāra's five vows as a young prince, all of which were fulfilled — receiving the throne, meeting an enlightened teacher (the Buddha), receiving Dharma, etc.

**Abstract**

A canonical narrative of King Bimbisāra's piety, demonstrating the principle that proper vow-making leads to the fulfillment of one's aspirations. Translation dated to Zhī Qiān's Wú productive period (222–252 CE). The text has parallels in the Pāli Vinaya and the *Saṃyutta-nikāya*.
